newsitem.title: UK: BT hails EU clearance for MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: BT hails EU clearance for MCI merger.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Wednesday welcomed the well-flagged clearance by European Commission regulators of its ambitious $20-billion merger with America's MCI Communications Corp.

BT and MCI made two minor concessions in order to clinch the regulatory green light, which included the sale of MCI's audioconferencing business in Britain -- the two companies have a dominant position here -- and selling some of their capacity on transatlantic cables.
"We're very pleased. They placed a couple of conditions on clearance and we were only too happy to agree to them," a company spokesman told Reuters.

Approval, which had been assured by European Competition Commissioner Karl Van Miert in a BBC radio interview on Tuesday night, means that U.S. regulatory clearance is the last hurdle in the creation of a new "global supercarrier" called Concert Plc.
BT says the definitive all-clear is on track for autumn.
The news failed to lift BT's shares, which have surged from around 380 pence to 466p since the propsed merger was announced last November. The stock closed at 499.5p, a loss of three pence.
"The EU clearance is entirely expected and the market as a whole is weaker," noted one telecoms analyst.
Concert, a telecoms giant with annual revenues of more than 25 billion stg and 43 million customers, will be floated on both the London and New York stock exchanges.
Concert will be the world's fourth-biggest telecoms group in terms of sales after Japans Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, America's AT&T Corp and Deutsche Telekom AG.
Analysts say the alliance appears to be the best-positioned global carrier in a rapidly consolidating global telecoms industry which is expected to be worth $1.0 trillion by 2000.
Its two rival partnerships are Global One, which links Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint and the Unisource/World Partners alliances formed by AT&T.
BT reports full-year results on Thursday and is expected to lift pre-tax profits to around 3.196 billion stg from 3.02 billion.
